chunks: Who are fearful of their Lord inwardly and dread the Hour.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to fear the Lord by the unseen (bil-ghayb)?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'bil-ghayb' (in the unseen) is often interpreted not merely as God's invisibility, but as the state of being unseen by people, highlighting the sincerity of the righteous who worship for God alone rather than for social recognition. This verse is frequently cited to illustrate the spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams, who maintained constant vigilance (muraqabah) and fear of the Hour even in private moments. The emphasis on 'mushfiqun' (anxious/expectant) underscores a dynamic, active faith rather than passive belief, linking inner piety directly to eschatological accountability.
